title: Man. Post. Cap. II GAR: inclination to like sins; not enough for alien imputation
pass_a_gloss: GAR. It is an inclination to sins like that first sin of Adam. Truly so; but also to Adam's other sins. Shall we therefore say the rest of Adam's sins likewise are imputed to us? Indeed it is by no means a sufficient cause of the imputation of another's sin that our sin incline and bend our mind the same way. For many have an inclination and a certain natural impulse toward similar sins of others, without any imputation of those at all. etc.
pass_b_english: Garissoles: It is an inclination to sins like Adam's first. True enough—but also to Adam's other sins. Shall we therefore say those other sins of Adam are likewise imputed to us? No: it is nowhere near enough, as a cause for imputing another's sin, that our sin bends our mind the same way. Many people have an inclination and a kind of natural push toward sins like other people's, with no imputation of those sins at all. And so on.
source_text: GAR. Est inclinatio ad peccata similia peccato illi primo Adae. Sane vero; Sed & ad alia Adami peccata. An ideo dicemus, reliqua itidem Adami peccata nobis imputari? Imo nequaquam sufficiens est alieni peccati imputationis causa, ut nostrum peccatum eodem animum nostrum inclinet & flectat. Multi enim inclinationem, & naturalem quendam impetum habent ad similia aliorum peccata, sine omni omnino illorum imputatione. &c.

choices.choice: Keep other-Adam-sins reductio and natural impetus without imputation
